ideas.risks: May only prove a black-box oracle barrier, not a represented PAC separation; if the oracle model is too strong or too weak, the result may not inform the atlas edge.
ideas.summary: Formalize the solver's obstruction as an explicit oracle model: the algorithm may adaptively query distributions or bounded losses and receives any hypothesis whose correlation is within fixed additive slack of the best concept correlation. Construct two indistinguishable worlds, one with best excess advantage about epsilon and one with no advantage, such that every polynomial-query booster sees only flat-region oracle answers.
ideas.title: Black-Box Fixed-Slack Barrier
ideas.why_promising: This isolates exactly what generic agnostic boosting cannot prove and gives a precise target for critics: either the lower bound is valid, or it reveals which non-black-box information a positive proof must exploit.

ideas.risks: The posterior threshold may be an artifact of the simple noisy-comparator model; adaptive relabeling or randomized filters may evade a one-label calculation.
ideas.summary: Turn the posterior-certification obstruction in the atlas note into a theorem. In a distribution where Y equals a hidden comparator corrupted at noise eta > gamma, analyze any observable filter/relabeling map based on k labeled examples and bound when the induced weak-learner query can have OPT_C < gamma without already containing significant information about the comparator.
ideas.title: Posterior Forcing Lemma
ideas.why_promising: A rigorous threshold theorem would sharply characterize the missing residual-amplification primitive and could rule out broad classes of observable filtering arguments.

ideas.risks: Known residual-free boosters may already imply this only with hidden exponential dependence; the explorer must track parameters rather than rediscover the near miss.
ideas.summary: Audit da Cunha-style fixed-slack residual-free boosting and related agnostic boosting theorems for the exact dependence on weak sample size, dual capacity, VC dimension, and representation size. Look for a special case or compression condition under which the candidate-generation menu becomes polynomial in 1/epsilon and representation size.
ideas.title: Parameter-Uniform Booster Audit
ideas.why_promising: The closest positive route is known to fail only quantitatively. A careful parameter audit may uncover a natural additional hypothesis yielding a conditional true theorem, or identify the exact exponential bottleneck to attack.

ideas.risks: It may collapse into known hard-core set or boosting machinery requiring a stronger oracle than OPT+beta; sampling clean witnesses may still be exponentially unlikely.
ideas.summary: Search for a polynomial clean-witness generator: given samples from a noisy distribution and a current predictor with excess more than epsilon, produce a polynomial list of reweighted or conditioned weak-learner query distributions such that one has OPT_C below gamma and any valid weak response yields measurable progress.
ideas.title: Polynomial Clean-Witness Generator
ideas.why_promising: This is the missing positive primitive named by previous runs. Framing it as list generation makes it separately testable and connects to compression, hard-core sets, and hitting-set methods.

ideas.risks: Distribution-free weak learning on all marginals is very demanding and may make the proposed gap class impossible; improper strong learning may exploit validation or public handles.
ideas.summary: Look for a represented class with a large-correlation-easy, small-correlation-hard gap. Candidate frameworks include SQ-hard planted correlation detection, LPN-like parities with a public high-advantage fallback, or cryptographic constructions where constant advantage is detectable but inverse-polynomial advantage is not. The key constraint is to verify the fixed OPT+beta weak learner for every distribution, not merely for a planted distribution family.
ideas.title: Large-Easy Small-Hard Separation Search
ideas.why_promising: A true negative edge needs exactly this phenomenon. The solver attempt clarifies why prior parity, halfspace, PRF, and handle templates fail, giving explorers concrete failure modes to avoid.

ideas.risks: Finite-domain experiments cannot prove the atlas implication; results may depend on nonuniform enumeration that is not representation-polynomial.
ideas.summary: Model small concept classes as finite matrices and solve LPs for fixed-slack weak oracle behavior versus strong agnostic mixtures. Search computationally for finite games where every fixed-slack oracle transcript can be uninformative while strong excess-error optimization requires epsilon-scale information. Extract candidate inequalities or impossibility patterns.
ideas.title: Finite Game LP Exploration
ideas.why_promising: Finite examples can expose the exact convex-analytic obstruction behind additive correlation floors and may suggest either a formal minimax barrier or a missing amplification inequality.
